newsitem.title: USA: First Team Q4 could be hurt by inventory.
newsitem.headline: First Team Q4 could be hurt by inventory.

text.p: First Team Sports Inc said Wednesday its results for the fourth quarter of fiscal 1997 could be hurt by high industry-wide inventory levels at retail.
Earlier, First Team reported lower earnings for the fiscal third quarter of $0.03 a share, down from $0.27 a year ago.

"Looking ahead to the fourth quarter of fiscal 1997, although our products had good sell-through during Christmas, there are still indications of continued high industry-wide inventory levels at retail which may affect fourth quarter re-order business," John Egart, president, said.

"The number of skate models First Team has placed at retail for the spring selling season is up significantly over last spring, and we look forward to shipping our new highly-anticipated product line in the first quarter of fiscal 1998," Egart added in a statement.
First Team makes in-line roller skates, accessories and roller hockey products.
The decline in third quarter earnings reflects lower sales for the quarter, which fell 26 percent to $16.7 million from $22.6 million a year ago.

"As mentioned in our preliminary release of December 17th, excess inventory and competitive pricing throughout the Christmas selling season impacted our earnings performance," Egart said. "This quarter was a continuation of the large inventory overhang from a slow spring and summer retail sales period for the in-line industry."
He added margins were significantly affected by sharp price reductions and subsequent markdowns at retail.
"However, we continue to manage our business very closely and take the proper steps to insure continuation of profitability and a strong balance sheet," Egart said.
He said the in-line skate industry suffered serious decreases in calendar 1996, but retailers have not backed away from supporting this category in 1997.

"According to the International In-Line Skating Association, in-line skating will continue to be one of the top three growing sports in America and retailers fully expect a rebound for next year," Egart said.
